title: Celebrate the Win rewrite - the team's findings (19 changes + 1 synthesized line)
linkLabel: Open the team run (all five voices)
summary:
Team you confirmed in chat at 7:13 PM: Walt Brennan (adversarial), Tasha Greene, Renee Calloway (standing seat), Marcus Lee, Priya Natarajan. Question: can someone who isn't like you read it once, understand it and use it? The page and the celebrate-the-win branch were NOT changed. Each change is its own question; no recommendations.

Walt's objection to the premise: "why is this on an AI site? ... The only AI sentence is the first line - and it's the line marked as made up."

The rewrite: https://github.com/level5consulting/ai-success-patterns/blob/ops/records/celebrate-the-win-rewrite-2026-11-19.md

questions.text: 1. Put the AI reason in "What goes wrong": AI work is invisible - nobody watched it get done, so nobody thanks anyone (Walt Brennan)
2. Replace "using 10 patterns" in step 1 with a business goal (Walt Brennan)
3. Either tell one of the "watched it happen twice" stories in a line, or drop the number (Walt Brennan)
4. Keep the page as short as it is now (Walt Brennan)
5. Add one example win a supervisor could use, e.g. "the monthly report takes two days instead of four" (Tasha Greene)
6. Step 2: say who to say it to - the team, the boss, or both (Tasha Greene)
7. Explain the Value Worksheet in half a sentence where it's mentioned (Tasha Greene)
8. Step 3: add "ask them" for when you don't know them well (Tasha Greene)
9. Move "at any regular check-in you already have" up as the easiest place to start (Tasha Greene)
10. Drop or explain the Notes at the bottom (ship-saver axiom, calcium for the bones) - they read like inside jokes (Tasha Greene)
11. Step 3: the leader does the thanking themselves - the booking can be delegated, the words can't (Renee Calloway)
12. Link step 1 to "When to use it": the person who set the goal checks it at the check-in they already have (Renee Calloway)
13. Say what comes off the coordinator's plate: no more quietly reminding the boss to thank people (Renee Calloway)
14. Step 2: some people want praise privately - ask (Marcus Lee)
15. Make the win about what people did, not about headcount, when the goal is "growing without adding people" (Marcus Lee)
16. "Half the team wasn't 21" -> "too young for a beer" (Marcus Lee)
17. "Celebrating a win is how they recover" -> "part of how they recover" (Marcus Lee)
18. Add a line for people working alone: mark it for yourself and thank anyone who helped (Priya Natarajan)
19. Add the solo reason to "Why it matters": if you never notice the time you got back, you fill it with more work (Priya Natarajan)

S1. [Synthesized] lead line: "When AI saves you time, nobody notices - including you. Decide up front what a win looks like, so you know when you hit one. Then stop and celebrate it with the people who made it happen."
When?
